claim_one_line: THE METRIC'S READ-OUT (the owner's goal of 2026-11-06, FL-05; data-free): the hyperbolic metric fixes, with no choice, a clock on the fibration circle -- harmonic time theta (the harmonic map in the fibre class; B1295's collocation generalised to any SnapPy holonomy, reproducing B1295's |c_(0,2)| = 4.260982635 exactly) -- and two weights on it: T1 the energy is UNIFORM in harmonic time on every member (coarea + Stokes; m004 chi2 38.6/39), T2 the volume weight rho has NO ATOM (theta real-analytic) -- so neither metric weight is a point on any member (Review 76, corrected: the metric's systole is a canonical point, and on L^6RLR it sits at the tube with the weight's peak). On the excursion member L^6RLR the volume weight is one hump (max/mean 1.75, min 0.81 at Rcut 12) centred exactly on the run's Margulis tube (shortest geodesic aaBa, 0.184870 - 0.802102i, chi = 0; theta == 0 on its core, the fixed set of the cyclic palindrome's isometry), confirmed by a second sampling through SnapPy's nine ideal tetrahedra, with the same theta (Bloch-Wigner volumes); flat on the golden m004 (0.98-1.03); sharper on L^10RLR (2.53). If a point is read, the metric ranks the closed thread's apex (the tube) over its anti-apex; if an average, it fixes the weight. The value of tau at the tube (apex 3.65, pleated 2.87, tetrahedron 2.58, or the level surface's own modulus) is NOT decided. 0 of 19.
